title: The standard projective linear action on lines
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $L=\mathrm{GL}_{I,k}$ be the general linear group scheme [def-sc-general-linear-group] with coordinate algebra $C=k[x_{ij},\det(x)^{-1}]$. Write $P=\operatorname{Proj} k[z_i:i\in I]$ over $k$, with total-degree grading [def-nagata-affine-proj, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; this projective space parametrizes lines in $k^I$. A left scheme action of $L$ on $P$ [def-sc-group-scheme] is the standard projective linear action if its morphism $L\times_kP\to P$, under the canonical affine base-change comparison $\operatorname{Proj} C[z_i]\simeq L\times_kP$, is induced by the graded ring map fixing $k$ and sending $z_i\mapsto\sum_jx_{ij}z_j$. The base-change comparison is characterized by its first projection being the structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and its second projection being Proj of the coefficient extension $k[z_i]\to C[z_i]$. Both graded maps have irrelevant-ideal images containing the target irrelevant ideal, so their Proj maps are defined on the entire scheme. This specifies the action on every test algebra, including nonreduced algebras, and also allows $I$ empty. This is a predicate on an action, not an assertion that one exists.
